messages.subject: while (.regexpr("\r", info) > 0) -- just solved a mind-boggling WinBUGS problem !
parts:
.... yes, WinBUGS :) It's still a perfectly good software, for many things.

So, I am using WB from R via "R2WinBUGS", and yesterday, when fitting some spatial CAR models, WB suddenly crashed with this obscure error message:

    Error in while (.regexpr("\r", info) > 0) { : argument is of length zero

For the CAR model, this was a crash. In contrast, with some other models (e.g., a simple linear regression), I got the same thing as a warning only, but WB continued to sample till the end and I got the results back into R. I googled the error message and found about two posts, but didn't really understand whether there was a solution.

So, I just tried one of the oldest methods in the book: I simply re-installed WinBUGS. And now it's working again ! So I assume I must have upset WB in some really deep way. I don't know what it is, but the new, clean installation seems to be fine again.

Just wanted to put this out there on the slight off-chance that any of you may (still use WB and) be faced with what to me was a mind-boggling problem.

Best regards  -- Marc
